activate-task-before-work.body:
Always call tasks__set_active before touching any file or reading code for a task — not after.

**Why:** Activating a task does two things: (1) it transitions status open→active so tasks__finish works cleanly at the end without DB workarounds, and (2) the LangGraph checkpoint starts injecting task context (body, decisions, history, related tasks, related commits) into every subsequent turn. That context makes the work better — Claude sees the plan, prior decisions, and related code chunks automatically. Skipping activation means working blind and then hitting gate errors at close time.

**How to apply:** The moment a task is identified for the current session, call tasks__set_active first — before reading files, before planning, before any edits. For multi-subtask work, activate each subtask in turn as you move to it.

activate-task-before-work.tags: task, set_active, activate, workflow, task-framework, context, checkpoint

always-activate-task-after-create.body:
Always call tasks__set_active immediately after tasks__create, in the same response.

**Why:** Memory injection into task_events (task-memory logging) only works when a task is active. Creating without activating means the first turns of work go untracked — no memory IDs, no turn history for that session.

**How to apply:** Any time tasks__create is called, follow it with tasks__set_active(task_id=<new_id>, session_id=<current_session_id>) before doing any other work.

anchor-heading-detection-regexes-to-line.body:
Any regex that detects a task-body section heading (e.g. "Resolution:", "## Files") by matching a literal word case-insensitively must anchor to the start of a line (`^` + re.MULTILINE, or an explicit "preceded by \n or start-of-string" check) — never a bare `re.search(r"(?i)word[: \t]*...")` with no position anchor.

Why: tasks__finish's resolution-unfilled gate (src/tools/tasks.py:916) used exactly this unanchored pattern. epic:f42b6958's Motivation section happened to contain the word "resolution" in ordinary prose ("namespaced by skill (meta, resolution, decisions[]...)"), which matched FIRST — before the real `Resolution:\nTBD` section later in the body — so the gate validated the wrong span of text and let a genuinely unfilled Resolution through undetected. Filed as epic:3792ba68.

How to apply: when writing or reviewing any body-parsing regex in this repo (section gates, `_BODY_FIELD_RE` in hooks/ui-adjacent code, grooming/introspection body detection), require the match to start at a line boundary. Test with a body whose OTHER sections contain the target heading word as ordinary prose — that's the exact case a bare case-insensitive search misses.

behavioral-steering-lives-in-skills-not-.body:
Epic 2f0fb672 (standing Execution Contract + per-tool Reflection loop, mechanical LangGraph/PostToolUse wiring) was abandoned 2026-07-05 — only its first prototype (task:380140fa, static Execution Contract injection at activation) shipped and stays.

Why: per-tool Reflection injection and a mechanical loop-detector would have required new PostToolUse/session_graph wiring for a problem that's really about behavioral steering, not state machinery. Decision: this class of guidance belongs in skill prose (improved /task-grooming, /task-introspection, and a new /task-implementation skill with behavioral guidelines), not in the LangGraph session design.

How to apply: future ideas for steering agent behavior mid-task (anti-drift, anti-looping, confidence checks, "when to stop exploring") should default to skill-prose additions first. Only reach for LangGraph/checkpoint/hook wiring if the mechanism genuinely requires cross-turn state that skill instructions can't carry on their own (the Execution Contract qualified because it needed to be injected identically every turn from the checkpoint; a reflection prompt doesn't need that).

check-uncommitted-diff-before-shipping-s.body:
Before running a deploy/merge pipeline from a shared dev worktree, run `git status --short` and inspect any uncommitted diff that isn't part of the current task -- don't assume it's broken or yours to discard, and don't ship it blindly either. In this case an unrelated uncommitted change (removing a dead function in hooks/server.py) turned out to be the tail end of an already-completed, already-committed task (its caller had already moved to dispatcher.py) -- verified via `git log --grep=<referenced task/bug id>` before committing it alongside the new feature.

Why: shared dev worktrees accumulate loose ends across sessions; a stale uncommitted diff can be either a forgotten completion of finished work (safe to include) or a broken half-edit (unsafe to ship) -- they look identical from `git status` alone.

How to apply: when `git status`/`git diff` in a shared worktree shows changes you didn't just make, grep the referenced task/bug id (in comments/docstrings) against git log and the task tracker before deciding whether to commit it, revert it, or leave it -- never silently include or silently discard.

check-uncommitted-diff-before-shipping-s.tags: git status uncommitted shared worktree dev deploy unrelated changes investigate before shipping task:15ee2da3

checkpoint-is-ipc.body:
SessionState flows between hooks via the LangGraph MemorySaver checkpoint (keyed by session_id/thread_id), not by re-reading sessions.db.

Rules:
- `run_session` (UPS) is the full state initializer. `_fresh_state` is a shared fallback also used by `run_gate` (PreToolUse) when no UPS checkpoint exists yet for the session.
- prompt_id, domains, keywords, memories are all in the checkpoint — gate_check and log_tool_usage read them from there, never from DB.
- set_prompt_id writes UUID to checkpoint only (no DB write mid-turn). sessions.db is written once at Stop via run_stop.
- pre_tool_use / run_gate is always fail-open — it never exits 2, even in dev mode.

**Why:** LangServe was stateless (each invoke discarded SessionState). MemorySaver (in-process, in-memory) replaced SqliteSaver in task:b3964f85 after two SqliteSaver corruption incidents — it keeps the graph as the cross-process-safe session store but does NOT persist across server restarts. `~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db` is a retired file nothing writes to anymore.
**How to apply:** When adding new hook logic that needs prior-turn data, read from state (it's in the checkpoint). Never add a DB read in gate_check or log_tool_usage. If no UPS checkpoint exists for a session, run_gate generates a fallback prompt_id (prefixed "fb-"). Remember checkpoint state is lost on server restart — don't assume it survives a /deploy restart.
checkpoint-is-ipc.name: checkpoint-is-ipc

checkpoint-session-cap-eviction-thrash.body:
`hooks__session_id` / `GET /session/current` returning "no checkpoint written yet" for a session that is clearly active and mid-conversation is usually NOT the hook server failing to fire for that session's cwd — it's checkpoint eviction. `_trim_checkpoints()` (hooks/server.py) keeps only the top `_CHECKPOINT_SESSION_CAP` most-recently-written thread_ids in `~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db`, and runs on EVERY `UserPromptSubmit` across ALL concurrent Claude Code windows/cwds sharing the one hook server — not just at server startup. So a long-running session in e.g. SeniorDevAgent's cwd can have its checkpoint wiped mid-conversation whenever sibling sessions in other cwds (claude-hooks-dev, vault, market-intel, etc.) each submit prompts and push it out of the top-N.

Raised cap from 2 → 5 on 2026-07-05 to reduce thrash with 3+ concurrent windows open. If `hooks__session_id` starts failing "most of the time" again, check how many Claude Code windows are open concurrently before assuming a code regression — it may just mean the cap needs raising further.

**Why:** Cost real confusion this session — looked like a bug/misconfiguration for a SeniorDevAgent-cwd session, was actually eviction thrash from other concurrent sessions.

**How to apply:** When `hooks__session_id` fails, check `_CHECKPOINT_SESSION_CAP` in hooks/server.py against how many Claude Code windows are typically open at once, rather than assuming the session/cwd isn't being tracked. The concept store entry `server-fastapi-hook-server` (module hooks/server.py) previously had a stale/wrong invariant claiming eviction happens at SessionEnd, not on every UserPromptSubmit — corrected 2026-07-05.

classify-domain-node-design.body:
ClassifyDomainNode (langchain_learning/nodes/classify_domain.py) loads domain_classifier.json from iCloud (src.config.domain_classifier_json) and uses full weighted scoring: strong/weak keyword signals, combination bigrams/trigrams, negative signals, and CWD map. Result feeds domains + skip_tools back into SessionState. Matched keywords from scoring are merged into state["keywords"] to enrich downstream BM25 in ScoreToolsNode. Score logging at INFO level shows top matched signals per domain. CWD signal comes from SessionState["cwd"] (threaded from hook input), not os.getcwd(). _DC_CACHE is module-level for one-load-per-process; invalidation via mtime check is a known TODO.

Why: Flat vocab set (_DOMAIN_VOCAB) was too coarse — no weighting, no phrases, no negative signals. The JSON config (externalized, iCloud-synced) is the authoritative source.
How to apply: When editing ClassifyDomainNode or domain_classifier.json, remember the CWD field must be in SessionState and passed from hook input. Keywords enrichment feeds score_tools — changes here affect tool hint retrieval.

The `claude` CLI supports `--safe-mode` (disables customizations/settings discovery) and `--tools ""` (empty string disables all tools; "default" enables all) as real, confirmed flags — verified via `claude --help` on 2026-07-04. Used in langchain_learning/subagent.py's BareClaudeAgent (safe_mode/no_tools constructor kwargs) for the task-context summarizer subprocess, so it runs as a pure text-in/text-out compressor with no tool access.

Why: needed a locked-down subprocess invocation of Claude for context summarization (task:b9dded3e) without inventing flags.

How to apply: reach for these flags whenever spawning a `claude -p` subprocess that should never read/write files or use tools — cheaper and more explicit than an empty settings.json alone (subagent.py already writes one for hook suppression, safe-mode/tools flags are the belt-and-suspenders addition).

Confirmed live (task:a91133b8, claude-hooks-dev's concept_store/extractor.py): a real call ignored `_SYSTEM`'s instruction and fenced the response anyway. Any code that does `json.loads()` directly on a `claude -p` completion needs to strip leading/trailing ` ``` ` (and an optional `json` language tag) first — don't trust the system prompt alone to prevent this. SeniorDevAgent's `loop/pass2.py::_parse_json` already has this fence-stripping (plus a `raw_decode` fallback for trailing prose) for object-shaped responses; claude-hooks-dev's `concept_store/extractor.py::_strip_json_response` is the array-shaped port of the same fix. Related: [[surface-design-tradeoffs-as-tasks-not-unilateral-fixes]].

claude-hooks-checkpointer-migration-pend.body:
task:b3964f85 SHIPPED 2026-07-09 (commit 4bcb560, dev→test via deploy.sh, live server confirmed running with "graph built with MemorySaver" in logs). hooks/server.py's lifespan now opens `MemorySaver()` instead of `SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(...)`. The old sqlite-specific `_trim_checkpoints`/`_compact_checkpoint_db` functions and `_CHECKPOINT_DB`/`_CHECKPOINT_SESSION_CAP`/`_CHECKPOINT_ROW_CAP` constants are DELETED from hooks/server.py — don't reference them, they no longer exist.

Per-thread checkpoint history is now capped at 5000 rows, enforced in `NoopNode.__call__` (langchain_learning/nodes/noop.py) on every Stop event via `_trim_thread_checkpoints()`, which reaches into `MemorySaver.storage`/`.writes` directly (checkpoint_ids are monotonically sortable strings, oldest evicted first). This mirrors the old cross-session sqlite trim's reliability rationale (run on an event that reliably fires every turn) but now bounds *per-thread* history in RAM, not *cross-thread* count in a sqlite file.

**Known follow-up gap, not yet addressed**: nothing currently caps the *number of distinct threads* MemorySaver keeps in RAM across the server's uptime — the old SqliteSaver-era `_CHECKPOINT_SESSION_CAP=5` cross-session eviction has no MemorySaver equivalent yet. Every session that has ever connected during this server's uptime stays in RAM until the next crash/restart. Low urgency today (KeepAlive crash-restarts and deploy.sh redeploys periodically clear everything anyway), but worth a task if the server ever runs stable for a very long time with many distinct sessions.

~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db (the corrupted file) renamed to langgraph_checkpoints.db.retired-2026-07-09 (not deleted, reversible) — alongside the pre-existing langgraph_checkpoints.db.old-bloated (1.7GB, from 2026-07-05). Neither is read by anything anymore; both are safe to hard-delete if reclaiming ~2.2GB matters, left for the user to decide.

**Confirmed drift caught and fixed by task:da29c842 (2026-07-27):** src/tools/hooks.py's `handle_checkpoint_query` was still reading raw sqlite3 from `~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db` — a leftover consumer of the retired file, throwing an unhandled "no such table: checkpoints" error since the file is now a 0-byte empty stub. Its docstring made the same now-false "SqliteSaver is production" claim this memory already warned about, dated with a since-superseded confirmation (task:61703ef7, 2026-07-05, predates this migration). Fixed: now a thin wrapper over `GET /session/{session_id}`, reading live MemorySaver state the same way hooks/server.py's own endpoints do. Lesson: a docstring/comment's "confirmed on <date>" claim is only as fresh as the last re-check against the code it describes — always grep for other direct `langgraph_checkpoints.db`/sqlite3 readers when touching checkpointer internals again, since this proves at least one straggler consumer can survive a migration undetected.

Any memory still asserting "production uses SqliteSaver" (langgraph-checkpointer-pattern, checkpoint-is-ipc, claude-hooks-session-lifecycle, claude-hooks-hook-delivery, claude-hooks-databases, claude-hooks-server-identity, session-id-how-to, checkpoint-session-cap-eviction-thrash, langgraph-sqlitesaver-direct-conn) is now STALE as of this shipped change — treat this memory as the authoritative current state, not those.

claude-hooks-code-rag-scope-decision.body:
Index the full repo (Python source + docs/) in code_rag — not docs-only.

**Why:** Empirically tested June 2024 — compared docs-only vs full-repo against 10 real task titles from the task DB. Full-repo won 7/10 by returning actual source locations (e.g., `load_memories.py:_bm25_fallback`) instead of doc sections. Implementation-oriented queries benefit most; the source chunk tells you *where to edit*, a doc section just tells you *what it does*.

**How to apply:**
- `build_code_embeddings.py` chunks `.py` files by AST top-level function/class and `.md` files in `docs/` by `##` section
- SKIP_DIRS excludes `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.git`, `node_modules`, `tests`
- `/gc` skill re-indexes changed `.py` and `.md` files after every commit
- Do not revert to docs-only — the comparison data justifies the extra index size
- If adding a new RAG scope (e.g. configs, scripts), default to including it rather than excluding

claude-hooks-commit-gate.body:
GitCommitGate (hooks/gates.py) blocks any Bash tool call containing `git commit` unless a `task:<id>` pattern appears anywhere in the command string (commit message body). Blocks with: 'Blocked: git commit is missing a task:<id> reference.' GitCommitMcpGate covers the MCP git__commit variant.

**Why:** Enforces traceability — every commit must reference an active task.
**How to apply:** Always pass task:<id> in the commit message body, or activate a task first with tasks__set_active.

claude-hooks-constraints.body:
Hooks must be fast and fail-open.

**How to apply:**
- `pre_tool_use` must never exit 2 (block) on error — always degrade gracefully
- All hooks degrade silently in prod mode if the server is unreachable
- No hook path should block Claude on a slow DB query, network call, or exception
- New nodes must be benchmarked — UPS target is under 300ms end-to-end

claude-hooks-context-token-budget.body:
UPS enforces a 4000-token budget (_CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET in hooks/dispatcher.py) across the 4 task-activation context categories (memories, related_tasks, related_commits, task_rag_chunks) before formatting the system prompt. Only `memories` gets trimmed on overflow — popped from the tail, since load_memories.py already returns it sorted descending by score with no cap. The other 3 categories are pre-capped at top-3 each and left untouched.

Why: memories was the only uncapped category and thus the only realistic source of a budget blowout; related_tasks/related_commits/task_rag_chunks are already small.

How to apply: if UPS context still exceeds budget in practice (visible via the ctx_tokens(...) fields in the UPS done sqlite log line), extend trimming to the other categories rather than assuming a bigger memories cap will fix it — see task:3de05199 and task:3369b86a for the logging/budget implementation.

claude-hooks-deploy-workflow.body:
Deployment is fully automated via /deploy skill — no need to know server details or run deploy.sh manually.

Workflow:
1. Edit in dev worktree (`~/workspace/claude-hooks-dev`)
2. Unit tests: `uv run python -m pytest tests/ -q -m 'not integration'`
3. Commit: `/gc`
4. Ship: `/deploy` — runs unit gate in dev, merges to test, restarts server via `launchctl kickstart -k`, runs full suite (unit + integration), then ships to main

Server log after restart: /tmp/claude-hooks-server.log

**Why:** Streamlined in June 2026 — /deploy skill wraps deploy.sh so no server knowledge required.
**How to apply:** Always use /deploy instead of running deploy.sh commands directly. To apply plist edits (not just a restart), run bootout + bootstrap instead — see memory: launchd-plist-reload-required.

claude-hooks-graph-event-routing.body:
Event routing in session_graph.py (one unified StateGraph for all 4 hook events):

- user_prompt_submit → load_turn → (task active?) → load_active_task → [tier-1 parallel] → summarize_task_context → [tier-2 parallel] → set_prompt_id → log_task_events → END
- pre_tool_use       → gate_check → END
- post_tool_use      → log_tool_usage → update_tool_keywords → (conditional bridge) → END

claude-hooks-load-memories-node.body:
LoadMemoriesNode retrieves top-5 memories via combination signal scoring (no embeddings, no external services):

Scoring per row:
  1. Domain weight   — project_domain=2.0 | global=0.5 | other=skip (0)
  2. Tag overlap     — Jaccard(prompt_tokens ∩ tag_tokens) × 3.0  (primary signal, hand-authored tags)
  3. Body overlap    — Jaccard(prompt_tokens ∩ body_tokens) × 1.0
  4. Recency boost   — ×1.2 if updated ≤30d, ×0.8 if ≥180d

All rows scanned (up to 500) in a single SQL read; scored in Python; top-5 returned.

Key behaviors:
- Global memories NOT auto-included — must earn a slot via keyword overlap (score 0.5 + overlap)
- Out-of-domain memories (neither project nor global) skip entirely — score=0
- No Ollama, no TurboVec, no iCloud read. Pure SQLite.

Tuning: when a wrong memory surfaces (visible in sqlite logs), tighten its tags. When a relevant memory is missed, add the right keyword to its tags. Tags are the primary retrieval lever.

claude-hooks-load-vault-context.body:
`_load_vault_context()` in `hooks/dispatcher.py` reads three LIFE_OS md files on every UserPromptSubmit turn and injects them as `## Soul context` in `additionalSystemPrompt`.

Files read (direct filesystem, no MCP):
- `~/workspace/claude_documents/LIFE_OS/soul.md` → "### Soul"
- `~/workspace/claude_documents/LIFE_OS/Debaditya.md` → "### Identity"

**Why:** Hermes-style always-on identity layer — complements BM25-scored SQLite memories with human-editable vault files. Always injected regardless of active task. Missing files are silently skipped (no caching, no complexity).

**How to apply:** Edit the three md files in Obsidian to update identity/soul/memory context. Do not add caching or conditional skipping logic — intentionally simple. Append durable notes via `vault__append` to `LIFE_OS/memory.md`.

claude-hooks-mission.body:
**Core goal: maintain context across long-running tasks** — Claude should never lose track of where a multi-session task stands, what decisions were made, and what's left. This is the reason the project exists.

claude-hooks is a LangGraph-based context injection system for Claude Code. It intercepts all four hook events (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) to build a persistent memory + session tracking layer around Claude.

**Mission:** make Claude context-aware across sessions — injecting relevant memories, tool hints, and session summaries automatically, without user intervention.

NODE_REGISTRY + get_node() factory keeps build_session_graph() as pure wiring. claude-hooks-observability-principle.body:
Debug from logs first — never from source code.

All hook events (UPS, PTU, PreTU, Stop), MCP tool calls, and node execution must be readable from `claude_hooks.sqlite` alone. If a behavior can't be diagnosed from log rows, that's a logging gap to fix.

**How to apply:**
- Every new node, handler, or MCP tool must emit INFO rows at entry/exit with timing and key state
- When debugging unexpected behavior: read logs first, grep source second
- Logging gaps (missing entry/exit rows) are bugs, not cosmetic issues

claude-hooks-posttooluse-bridge.body:
PostToolUse conditional bridge nodes react to specific MCP tool calls and write to the LangGraph checkpoint:

- tasks__set_active / tasks__pop_active  → ActivateTaskNode → (conditional) BackfillMemoryFilesNode
  ActivateTaskNode writes active_task_id, task_memories, task_files, active_task_domain, execution_contract to checkpoint.
  execution_contract (task:380140fa, 2026-07-05) is a fixed north-star template string built by _build_execution_contract(task_id, title) — rendered verbatim into the system prompt every turn while the task is active, deliberately exempt from _enforce_context_budget eviction and _TASK_BODY_CHAR_CAP truncation (see [[claude-hooks-context-token-budget]]).
  If task_files is non-empty, BackfillMemoryFilesNode runs after — backfills memories.files=NULL for
  domain-matched memories using stem-token overlap (LIMIT 5 per activation).
  BackfillMemoryFilesNode is the default BackfillNodeProtocol slot — swappable by rewiring the graph.
  Skipped for replay-* and test-* sessions.
- tasks__clear_active / tasks__finish    → DeactivateTaskNode — zeros active task in checkpoint, including execution_contract
- tasks__add_decision                    → DecisionTaskNode   — appends to mid_task_decisions in checkpoint

Rule: MCP tools never write to checkpoint directly — bridge nodes are the only path.

claude-hooks-recency-pull.body:
The system will always be drawn toward the latest task, freshest session, most recent signal. Resist this.

**What recency pull looks like — recognize and resist:**
- Refining scoring pipeline indefinitely instead of advancing tools.db or task ancestry
- Cleaning up memories or CLAUDE.md instead of advancing tool saturation (task:4d50496b)
- Adding observability polish beyond boundary correctness
- Working on the most recent bug without checking if it serves the mission
- Any session where no open task from the backlog was advanced

**The test:** at the end of a session, did the work move the mission forward, or did it just service the present moment?

When in doubt, re-read [[claude-hooks-mission]] and [[claude-hooks-open-work]] before starting a new task.

**Why:** SessionStart and SessionEnd are unreliable — not guaranteed to fire on crashes, force-quits, reconnects, or abnormal exits. UPS fires on every user turn, is synchronous, and blocks until it returns.

claude-hooks-session-lifecycle.body:
Session state is stored in SqliteSaver at ~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db keyed by session_id. State survives server restarts.

Checkpoint cap: `_trim_checkpoints()` runs on every UserPromptSubmit — keeps the 5 most recently active sessions (`_CHECKPOINT_SESSION_CAP=5`, raised from 2 on 2026-07-05 — task:d2c347ca — to reduce eviction thrash with 3+ concurrent Claude Code windows), evicts the rest. This ensures stale sessions never accumulate regardless of server uptime.

Stop fires every turn and must never evict checkpoints — doing so would wipe cross-turn state like prompt_tools and session_tools needed by gates.

**Why:** SessionEnd is unreliable (not guaranteed on crash/force-quit). UPS is the only hook that fires consistently every turn, so checkpoint hygiene lives there.

claude-hooks-skill-mcp-pattern.body:
Skills are the UI layer; MCP tools are the API layer; databases are storage. Each skill action maps to one or more MCP tool calls — analogous to a UI action calling multiple API endpoints in full-stack dev.

Example: /pause (skill/UI) → tasks__pause (MCP tool/API) → proj_tasks.db (storage)

**Why:** keeps skills thin (behavior contracts only) and MCP tools reusable, testable, and semantically named in logs. Raw tasks__update with manual markdown in a skill is a smell — if a skill repeats a formatting pattern, extract it into a dedicated MCP tool.

**How to apply:** when adding a new skill action that writes structured data, ask whether the write deserves its own MCP tool with a clean signature rather than a generic tasks__update/memory__add call.

claude-hooks-stop-vs-sessionend.body:
Stop hook fires at the end of EVERY assistant response — not at session end. Never do session-scoped cleanup on Stop — it wipes cross-turn state every turn.

SessionEnd and SessionStart are unreliable — not guaranteed to fire on crashes, force-quits, or reconnects. Do NOT rely on them for critical logic.

**Correct wiring:**
- Stop → finalise turn only (no eviction)
- SessionEnd → unreliable, do not depend on it
- UPS → checkpoint trim runs here (5-session cap enforced on every prompt, raised from 2 on 2026-07-05 — task:d2c347ca)

**Why:** Checkpoint hygiene was moved from SessionEnd to UPS precisely because SessionEnd cannot be trusted to always fire.

claude-hooks-task-state-machine.body:
Task status state machine, verified against src/tools/tasks.py (_VALID_STATUSES, _TRANSITIONS, is_valid_transition):

_VALID_STATUSES = {open, done, abandoned, blocked} — 'active' is NOT a DB status, see [[tasks-active-status-checkpoint-only]].

_TRANSITIONS:
  open    → {done, blocked}
  done    → {} (terminal)
  abandoned → {} (terminal)
  blocked → {open}

Any status → abandoned is always allowed (special-cased in is_valid_transition, not in the _TRANSITIONS dict). Same-status is always a no-op allow.

handle_update() in src/tools/tasks.py is the ONLY path for status transitions — it calls is_valid_transition() to enforce the machine. Nodes must NEVER run `UPDATE open_tasks SET status=...` directly — bypasses the guard and breaks gate enforcement.

**Correction (2026-07-05):** previous version of this memory claimed "open → active → done" and "active → open (requeue)" / "blocked → active (unblock)" — 'active' has never been a DB status; that was drift from confusing the DB status machine with the LangGraph checkpoint's active_task_id tracking. Verified directly against the _TRANSITIONS dict in code, not against another memory.

Integration tests use pytest fixtures that inject test-prefixed session IDs to avoid polluting prod DBs.

**How to apply:** Never use a real session ID in integration tests — always use a test-prefixed ID.

claude-hooks-tool-tracking.body:
PostToolUse runs log_tool_usage node which does 3 things concurrently via ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2):
1. Upserts tool_hints.sqlite — increments count, updates rolling avg latency, appends prompt to recent_prompts (last 10 kept), seeds keywords from tool name tokens + domain if empty
2. Appends tool name to task_events.tools for current prompt_id in proj_tasks.db
3. Updates prompt_tools and session_tools in LangGraph checkpoint

Gate prereq checks read prompt_tools/session_tools from checkpoint — tool names are MCP-prefix-stripped so both gate and log see the same short name.

claude-hooks-type-vocabulary.body:
Two DIFFERENT type vocabularies in the task system — easy to confuse:

- body `Type:` ∈ {feature, bug, research, misc, epic} — workflow kind, controls required body sections.
- `issue_type` param ∈ {epic, story, task, bug, subtask, feedback} — DB hierarchy (verified against _ISSUE_TYPES in src/tools/tasks.py).

`issue_type='task'` or `'story'` REQUIRES a parent (JiraHierarchyGate) — a standalone/root task must use `issue_type='epic'`. `issue_type='subtask'` requires a parent of type {bug, story, task} — not epic. `issue_type='feedback'` is created via tasks__create_feedback, always parented to a finished task.

claude-hooks uses three git worktrees for a proper SDLC:

- `~/workspace/claude-hooks-dev` → `dev` branch — all edits, quick unit tests, `/gc` commits
- `~/workspace/claude-hooks-test` → `test` branch — server runs here (port 8766, no --reload); full test suite runs against this
- `~/workspace/claude-hooks` → `main` branch — sacred, only receives clean merges via `/deploy`

**Deploy flow:** Use `/deploy` skill — runs unit gate in dev, merges dev→test, restarts the server via `launchctl kickstart -k`, runs full suite, then ships test→main.

**Why:** Server runs from test worktree so dev edits never disrupt live Claude Code hooks. Main is never touched directly.

**How to apply:** All edits go in dev. Never edit test or main directly. Use `/deploy` to ship.

claude-hooks-worktree-test.body:
The claude-hooks test worktree at `~/workspace/claude-hooks-test` (test branch) is where the hook server runs.

Launchd plist WorkingDirectory: `~/workspace/claude-hooks-test`. Server runs without --reload on port 8766. deploy.sh restarts it via `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/<plist-label>` after merging dev→test, then health-checks before running the full suite.

Integration and UI tests (pytest -m integration) hit this server via HTTP — they work from any worktree.

**Why:** Isolates the live server from in-progress dev edits. Main is never the server source.

**How to apply:** After /deploy merges dev→test and restarts the server, integration tests run against fresh code. Never point the plist at dev or main. Check /tmp/claude-hooks-server.log if server fails to come up.

**Note:** `launchctl kickstart -k` restarts the process but uses launchd's in-memory plist config. To apply plist edits, run bootout + bootstrap (see memory: launchd-plist-reload-required).
claude-hooks-worktree-test.name: claude-hooks-worktree-test

concept-evidence-use-code-snippet-not-li.body:
When recording `evidence` entries in concept_store/concepts.json, prefer a stable code snippet (e.g. the literal `builder.add_edge("load_turn", "cache_check")` call) over a file:line pointer.

Why: line numbers drift whenever comments or unrelated code get added above the referenced line — the pointer silently goes stale even though the underlying fact is still true. A grep-able snippet stays correct regardless of surrounding edits.

How to apply: when adding or updating a concept's evidence field (during /deploy's concept audit, task-introspection's concept-store audit, or ad hoc updates), use `"<module path>: <exact code substring>"` instead of `"<module path>:<line>"`. Existing line-number evidence doesn't need a mass migration — fix opportunistically when touched.

concepts.json edits are documentation-only (no runtime effect) — they don't need to go through /deploy's dev→test→main pipeline urgently; fine to batch with the next code change.

cwd-first-fallback-default-repo-pattern.body:
UPS pipeline nodes that resolve a repo-scoped index/resource must try `state["cwd"]`'s repo first, falling back to a default repo (claude-hooks) only if nothing exists there — never hardcode a single repo. `load_task_code.py` established this pattern; `load_related_commits.py` was fixed to match it (bug task:4b7ccfe8).

Why: a task can be activated from any repo, not just claude-hooks-dev/-test/-main. A node that skips the cwd check doesn't fail loudly on a cross-repo task — it silently returns data from the wrong repo (e.g. claude-hooks commits injected as "related" for an ecommerce-blast-radius task), which is worse than returning nothing. Design intent: a task should behave the same way regardless of which repo it lives in.

How to apply: when adding a new UPS node that reads a repo-local file/index (TurboVec .tvim, git log, etc.), resolve the path as `Path(state["cwd"]) / <resource>` first; only fall back to a fixed default path if the cwd-scoped resource doesn't exist. Apply this check whenever reviewing or adding fan-out nodes in langchain_learning/nodes/.

dead-code-survives-task-completion.body:
When a later task/refactor supersedes an earlier task's implementation (e.g. moving logic from a bare function into a properly-logged dispatcher handler), the old function can be left behind as dead code even after the newer code is confirmed working in production logs — and the original task can stay open/pending indefinitely since nobody circles back to close it once the goal is de facto met elsewhere.

Why: found via this exact pattern in claude-hooks-dev: hooks/server.py had a bare `_evict_session()` (no dispatcher logging) sitting unreferenced since before task c05204ac, while the actual live route called dispatcher._handle_session_end — which fulfilled c05204ac's stated goal (SessionEnd eviction + logging) as an incidental side effect of a different task (b7cb4eb4/c2a8f350). The task was never marked done and the dead function was never deleted.

How to apply: when investigating "who does X" or "is this still used" during a debugging/exploration session, grep for the function name across the repo before trusting a docstring or an open task's description — an open task doesn't mean the work wasn't done, and a documented function doesn't mean it's live. Cross-check open tasks whose described goal matches code you've already found working elsewhere; they're often stale-open rather than actually blocked.
dead-code-survives-task-completion.name: dead-code-survives-task-completion
dead-code-survives-task-completion.tags: dead code, task hygiene, task status, superseded implementation, cleanup, orphaned function, task:c05204ac

debug-mode-rca-pattern.body:
Switch log level to DEBUG during root cause analysis — no code change needed.

All nodes emit debug logs for skip paths and candidate evaluation. sqlite_log_handler.py writes at whatever level the root logger emits, so debug traces land in claude_hooks.sqlite automatically when DEBUG is active.

**Why:** Debug logs are structured but verbose — always present in code, suppressed at INFO in prod. Flipping to DEBUG during an incident surfaces the full trace without adding temporary print statements or redeploying.

**How to apply:** When a feature produces unexpected 0-count or silent-skip behaviour (e.g. backfill_memory_files writing nothing), enable DEBUG on the root logger for the session and re-read logs via mcp__claude-hooks__hooks__read_logs_sqlite. Look for skip-reason and candidate-count lines to pinpoint the failure point.
debug-mode-rca-pattern.name: debug-mode-rca-pattern

deploy-concept-audit-catches-what-groomi.body:
The /deploy skill's Step 1 concept audit (diffing changed modules against concept_store invariants right before shipping to test) caught a real integration gap during task:850ddd65 that /task-grooming's pre-implementation pass had no way to catch: the new ## Repo memories context section bypassed _enforce_context_budget's token accounting entirely, silently violating the dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly concept's stated invariant.

Why grooming couldn't have caught this: grooming runs BEFORE implementation, when the exact shape of new code (a new context section, a new state field) isn't concretely known yet — it can flag general risk areas but can't diff against code that doesn't exist yet. The concept audit runs AFTER implementation, against the actual diff, immediately before the change goes live — structurally the last point where a stored invariant can be checked against real changed files.

This is why both checks matter and aren't redundant: grooming catches premise/design gaps early (cheap to fix), concept audit catches implementation-vs-invariant drift late (last chance before shipping). Don't skip the deploy skill's concept audit step thinking grooming already covered it — they catch different classes of problems at different points in the lifecycle.
deploy-concept-audit-catches-what-groomi.name: deploy-concept-audit-catches-what-grooming-misses
deploy-concept-audit-catches-what-groomi.tags: deploy, concept audit, task-grooming, invariant, integration gap, lifecycle, context budget

deploy-skip-tests-md-only.body:
Don't run the unit/integration test suite as part of /deploy when the dev→test diff is markdown-only (e.g. README changes). Merge straight through instead.

Why: user pointed out mid-deploy that running the full 602-unit + 69-integration suite for a 4-line README addition is wasted time — markdown changes can't break behavior the suite checks.

How to apply: before invoking ~/workspace/claude-hooks/scripts/deploy.sh, check `git diff origin/test --name-only`. If every changed path ends in .md, merge dev→test and test→main directly without running the full gate. If the diff mixes .md with .py/other code files, still run the full suite — only skip when the diff is markdown-only.

dev-gate-removal-task-close-gotcha.body:
When removing a gate from dev, MCP tool calls that pass through the running test server will still be blocked by the OLD gate until /deploy is run.

**Why:** The test server (claude-hooks-test worktree, port 8766) runs the code from the test branch. Dev edits don't affect it until merged via deploy.sh. So if you remove a gate in dev and then try to call an MCP tool that the old gate blocks, it will fail — even though the new code no longer has the gate.

**How to apply:** After removing a gate in dev, don't try to use MCP tools that the removed gate was blocking (e.g. tasks__finish for tasks stuck in "open" due to old review gate). Either: (a) write directly to the DB as a workaround, or (b) /deploy first so the test server picks up the new gate-free code. Flag this clearly rather than debugging the MCP error as if it's a code bug.

diff-before-copying-assumed-source-of-tr.body:
Before `cp`-ing a file to "sync" it from a supposed source-of-truth location to another copy, diff them first — don't assume the source path is actually current just because it's "the repo copy."

Why: mid-session, a correctly-fixed `~/.claude/skills/deploy/skill.md` (edited directly, twice, for two separate bugs) got silently overwritten by `cp ~/workspace/claude-hooks/skills/deploy/skill.md ~/.claude/skills/deploy/skill.md` — the repo copy looked authoritative but was actually stale (it lacked `repo:`/`deployed:` frontmatter entirely, meaning nobody had a documented sync convention for that file, and it had silently drifted for weeks). The overwrite wasn't caught until a system-reminder surfaced the post-copy diff.

How to apply: before any `cp`/sync operation intended to propagate a fix, run `diff` between source and destination first and read it — if the destination has newer-looking content the source lacks (recent task IDs, dated language), stop and reconcile manually rather than trusting file-path conventions alone. This is the same root lesson as [[skills-live-in-both-main-and-dev-worktree]] and [[git-local-sh-y-stages-everything]] — assumed "this path is the source of truth" without verifying it, twice in one session with two different mechanisms (git add -A, and a manual cp).
diff-before-copying-assumed-source-of-tr.name: diff-before-copying-assumed-source-of-truth

docstrings-can-claim-unbuilt-integration.body:
A module docstring can describe an integration that was planned/aspirational but never actually built — don't trust a docstring's claim about "who calls this" without grepping for the actual call site.

Why: prompt_cache.py's docstring named happiest-minds-tracker as a consumer of the cache; grepping the skill found zero calls to prompt_cache__lookup/__store — the claim was aspirational, not descriptive.

How to apply: when a docstring/comment asserts a specific caller or integration point, verify with a grep/Explore pass before relying on it for debugging or design decisions — especially when investigating "why didn't X happen" bug reports.

docstrings-improve-rag-chunks.body:
Add meaningful docstrings to all high-level functions, endpoints, and classes so code RAG retrieval surfaces the right chunks for task-related queries.

**Why:** The RAG chunker splits by function/section. Bare functions (no docstring) produce chunks with no semantic signal beyond the name — they won't surface for task queries even when they're the most relevant file. Adding docstrings with key domain terms (e.g. `gate_check`, `permissionDecision`, `name_arg_check`, `claude_hooks.sqlite`) pulls those chunks into top-5 results. Validated: `hooks/server.py` `pre_tool_use` went from absent to #2 (0.748) after docstrings were added.

**How to apply:** When writing or editing any function that owns a meaningful behavior (endpoints, node `__call__`, gate `verify`, dispatcher handlers), add a one-to-three line docstring covering: what it does, what it returns, and any key domain terms (tool names, log fields, DB names) that someone searching for this behavior would use. Especially important for FastAPI endpoints and LangGraph nodes — they're the most-queried entry points.
docstrings-improve-rag-chunks.name: docstrings-improve-rag-chunks

domain-classifier-llm-when.body:
Use use_llm=True (Haiku via ChatAnthropic) for domain classification on long-running new projects where semantic understanding matters more than speed.
Why: keyword path misses semantic matches (e.g. "knee pain" → health); Haiku understands intent. Cost (~300ms + API) is acceptable when amortized over a long session.
Use use_llm=False (keyword default) for hooks and short-lived invocations where latency and offline reliability matter.
How to apply: when starting a new project pipeline, consider enabling use_llm=True in build_memory_pipeline(). For the memory_loader hook, always keep keyword default.

every-task-skill-needs-quantified-delive.body:
Every task-* skill should produce some quantified output as its deliverable, not just prose/checklists.

Existing coverage: /task-grooming quantifies via document.grooming.risks[]/clarifications/hidden_assumptions counts ("N gaps found"). /task-introspection quantifies via document.grooming_accuracy tallies (predicted/materialized/avoided/wrong). /task-create and /task-framework are creation/orchestration — arguably don't need one.

Gap: /task-implementation currently has NO quantified deliverable — only the Resolution: checklist ticks in the body, which aren't rolled up anywhere structured in [[task-document-schema]]. User explicitly wants this left as-is for now (2026-07-26) rather than adding a new document.implementation namespace, due to overlap risk with tasks__add_decision/task_events and friction-during-flow risk (implementation is continuous work, not a discrete bookend call like grooming/introspection).

How to apply: next time /task-implementation or the task-document schema is revisited, propose a minimal quantified metric for implementation (e.g. checklist items completed / total, or tests passed count) rather than a full parallel structure to grooming/introspection — keep it a single number/tally, not a growing log, to avoid the flow-friction tradeoff already discussed and rejected once.

exclude-active-session-from-live-index-b.body:
When capturing a regression baseline against a live append-only index, exclude sessions that are still actively generating events.

**Why:** `score_tools` reads from `tool_hints.sqlite`, which grows with every PostToolUse event. The current session's tool count at capture time T differs from what replay sees at T+N seconds — after more tool calls have been logged. All completed sessions have a frozen tool history; only the active session is a moving target. This caused `test_replay_matches_baseline` to fail on every deploy.

**How to apply:** In `replay_harness.py`, `_active_session_ids()` detects sessions whose last UPS event is within 30 minutes and `cmd_capture()` skips them. The general principle: any regression baseline scored against a live index must exclude in-flight sessions — detect them by recency (last event age < threshold), not by an explicit end marker (end markers are unreliable).

feedback-fix-in-dev-first.body:
Always fix issues in the dev worktree first, even when the bug is discovered in test or main.

**Why:** Dev is the only place changes should originate — test and main are downstream. Fixing directly in test/main breaks the dev→test→main pipeline and risks divergence.

**How to apply:** When a test failure or bug surfaces during deploy (unit gate, full suite, or post-ship), stop, go to dev, fix there, commit via /gc, then re-run /deploy from the top.

file-token-matching-stem-only.body:
When tokenizing file paths for name/tag overlap matching, use only the filename stem — not directory components. `hooks/gates.py` → {gate, gates}, not {hook, hooks, gate, gates}.

**Why:** Directory names (hooks, src, tests, langchain) appear in nearly every memory slug in the domain, causing false-positive matches. A memory named `claude-hooks-unrelated-foo` would match any file under `hooks/` if directory tokens were included.

**How to apply:** In `_file_tokens()`, split only the last path component (after the final `/`), strip the extension, then split on `_` and `-`. Add naive plural/singular variants. Never call `re.findall` on the full path string.

fixed-sleep-vs-poll-loop-after-timing-ch.body:
Any fixed `sleep N` waiting for a process to become ready is a timing assumption that silently depends on startup staying fast — it isn't robust, it's just been lucky so far. Adding literally any new startup-time work (even something as small as a 2.4s checkpoint DB compaction) can push real startup time past the sleep, and the failure mode is immediate: "server unreachable" on a server that's actually fine, just slightly slower to boot.

**Why:** `scripts/deploy.sh`'s `sleep 3` after `launchctl kickstart -k` had worked reliably for a long time. Adding `_compact_checkpoint_db()` to server startup (task:b623ea48) pushed boot time past 3s consistently, and the fixed-sleep health check started failing on every single deploy — the server was healthy, just not within 3 seconds.

**How to apply:** Prefer a poll loop (retry health check every 1s, up to some generous ceiling) over any fixed sleep before checking whether a process/service is ready — costs nothing extra when things are fast, and doesn't need re-tuning every time startup work changes. When a fixed sleep exists in a deploy/CI script, treat it as a latent bug waiting for the next person to add startup work, not a settled constant.
fixed-sleep-vs-poll-loop-after-timing-ch.name: fixed-sleep-vs-poll-loop-after-timing-change
fixed-sleep-vs-poll-loop-after-timing-ch.tags: deploy.sh, fixed sleep, poll loop, health check, startup time, timing assumption

gate-policy-boundary-in-node.body:
GateCheckNode has two distinct responsibilities — keep them separate:
  1. State transformation: extract tool_name, build GateContext from SessionState (stays in node)
  2. Policy decision: check(tool_name, ctx) → (deny, reason) (delegated to GatePolicy)

The GATES early-return (`if tool_name not in GATES`) also stays in the node — it is routing logic (skip ungated tools), not policy logic.

**Why:** GateContext construction involves ~30 lines of state extraction. It is not part of the policy contract — a different policy impl would still need the same GateContext. Mixing them would make every policy reimplementer rebuild the extraction logic.

**How to apply:** When adding a new Protocol boundary to a node, ask: 'would every alternative implementation need to redo this code?' If yes, it stays in the node. If no, it belongs in the Protocol impl.
gate-policy-boundary-in-node.name: gate-policy-boundary-in-node
gate-policy-boundary-in-node.tags: gate policy protocol GateCheckNode GateContext state transformation boundary separation

gate-rules-yaml-schema.body:
~/.claude/gate_rules.yaml schema:

  tool:      (required) short tool name, e.g. imessage__send
  prereq:    (required) tool that must have been called recently
  window_s:  seconds to look back (default 120)
  name_arg:  key in the PREREQ tool's input whose value must appear in the prompt
  input_arg: key in the GATED tool's own input whose value must appear in the prompt

name_arg and input_arg are mutually exclusive in practice:
- name_arg: used when prereq is a lookup (contacts__search name='Alice')
- input_arg: used when the relevant value is on the gated call itself (mail__compose to='x@y.com')

**How to apply:** Check existing entries as reference. input_arg check runs before prereq scan — fail fast.
gate-rules-yaml-schema.name: gate-rules-yaml-schema
gate-rules-yaml-schema.tags: gate rules yaml schema name_arg input_arg prereq config external task:84e4fc39

gates-config-driven-external-tools.body:
External MCP tool gates (local-mac tools like imessage__send, mail__compose, mail__delete) are declared in ~/.claude/gate_rules.yaml — not as Python classes in gates.py. The loader _load_external_gates() reads the YAML at module import and merges into GATES. Internal gates (git, tasks — need DB access) stay as code.

**Validated end-to-end (2026-07-05), twice independently:**
1. imessage__send: contacts__search(name="Alice") logged into session_tools, then gate_check's name_arg_check found name='alice' in the recent prompt text → ALLOW → message sent.
2. mail__delete: mail__read (from ~42s earlier, same session) satisfied the plain prereq check via session-wide lookback → ALLOW → delete succeeded.

Both are the first real end-to-end firings of this mechanism in the repo's log history — prior to this it had only ever been observed registering at import, never actually evaluating a real gated call.

**Gotcha caught while validating:** gate_check's DEBUG log line `current=[...]` (from GateContext.current_calls) is scoped to only the current prompt/turn — it is NOT what the prereq check actually reads. The real prereq lookback (_make_prereq_check → ctx.prev_tools()) draws from session_tools, which spans the whole session across all prior prompts/turns within window_s. Seeing `current=[]` on a gated call does NOT mean the prereq was missing — check prev_tools()/session_tools timestamps against window_s instead, not the current_calls debug field, before concluding a gate failed to enforce its prereq.

**Why:** McpHookBridgeNode pattern — engine in claude-hooks, rules owned by the tool's repo/config. No Python change needed to gate a new external tool.

**How to apply:** To gate a new local-mac tool, add an entry to ~/.claude/gate_rules.yaml with tool, prereq, window_s, and optionally name_arg or input_arg. Never add a concrete Gate subclass for an external tool. Don't assume "registered at startup" means "actually exercised" — same lesson as [[summarize-task-context-never-actually-fired]] — but for this specific mechanism, it's now confirmed both to load AND to correctly gate two different real calls.
gates-config-driven-external-tools.name: gates-config-driven-external-tools
gates-config-driven-external-tools.tags: external gates, gate_rules.yaml, imessage__send, mail__delete, contacts__search, validated, end-to-end, local-mac, session-wide prereq lookback

git-local-sh-y-stages-everything.body:
`git_local.sh -y` stages ALL pending changes in the repo, not just the files passed to a preceding `git add <files>` — running `git add fileA fileB && git_local.sh -y "msg"` still swept in an unrelated uncommitted CLAUDE.md edit that was never `git add`ed.

Why: discovered while trying to split a session's changes into two targeted commits (a bugfix and a separate docs tweak) per [[gc]]'s "grouping changes into multiple commits" guidance — the intended split silently didn't happen; both landed in the first commit.

How to apply: when the [[gc]] skill's grouping guidance calls for separate commits, don't rely on `git add <specific files>` immediately before `git_local.sh -y` to scope the commit — either commit the unrelated change first as its own commit, or verify with `git show --stat HEAD` right after committing that only the intended files landed, and unwind/re-split if not. Low-stakes when both changes are correct and coherent (as here), but would matter more for a commit that's supposed to exclude something.

gitcommitgate-false-positive-on-git-name.body:
GitCommitGate's regex (git\s+(?:(?!commit\b)\S+\s+)*commit\b) can false-positive on a Bash call that never invokes `git commit` at all, if the command text happens to contain the literal token "git" (e.g. a Python variable named `git`) followed later by a whole-word "commit" (e.g. inside "pre-commit", since a hyphen counts as a word boundary).

Why: the regex scans the raw Bash command string for token proximity, not actual shell command structure — it can't distinguish a real `git commit` invocation from these tokens coincidentally appearing in unrelated script content (e.g. building a markdown table description that mentions "pre-commit tests").

How to apply: when embedding Python/other scripts inside a Bash tool call, avoid naming variables `git`, and be aware that other tool descriptions mentioning both words could occasionally trip this gate too. If a Bash call is unexpectedly denied for git commit despite not running one, check the raw command string for coincidental "git ... commit" token proximity before assuming the gate itself is broken.
gitcommitgate-false-positive-on-git-name.name: gitcommitgate-false-positive-on-git-named-variable
gitcommitgate-false-positive-on-git-name.tags: gitcommitgate, false positive, bash tool, regex, git commit gate, variable naming, pre-commit, task:bfccbf36

gitignore-rag-files.body:
Always add RAG/embedding index files to .gitignore — never commit them.

**Why:** These are derived artifacts (rebuilt on demand or server startup) and should not be tracked. Files include: `.code_embeddings.tvim`, `.code_embeddings.meta.json`, `.tasks_embeddings.tvim`, `.tasks_embeddings.meta.json`, `.diff_embeddings.tvim`, `.diff_embeddings.meta.json`.

**How to apply:** Whenever creating a new RAG pipeline or embedding index, immediately add its output files to `.gitignore` before any commits.
gitignore-rag-files.name: gitignore-rag-files

grep-all-md-files-before-declaring-doc-r.body:
When stripping documentation for a removed feature, grep ALL .md files repo-wide for the feature's key symbol names before declaring the doc-removal pass complete — don't trust the task's named file list (e.g. "CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md").

Why: task:0537e805 was scoped to 2 files; a repo-wide grep for cache_check/prompt_cache/CacheCheckNode turned up 3 more files with the same stale topology diagram or live instruction duplicated (.github/copilot-instructions.md — 5 separate mentions; docs/arch/task_framework.md — a topology diagram; task_templates/research.md — a LIVE task-template instruction that would have kept injecting a dead-tool reference into every future research task if missed).

How to apply: for any "remove feature docs" task, run `grep -rln <feature_symbols> --include='*.md' .` across the whole repo as the first step, not the last.

grep-repo-wide-for-old-behavior-signatur.body:
When refactoring away an old behavior (e.g. a specific API response shape, a removed field, a deleted function), grep the whole repo for that behavior's identifying string/signature before considering the refactor done -- not just the unit test co-located with the file you changed. An end-to-end test file (test_hooks_lc.py) asserting the same old response shape (decision=="block") was missed on the first pass because only the directly-adjacent unit test (test_noop_node.py) was checked, causing an avoidable deploy.sh failure on the first attempt.

Why: behavior can be asserted in multiple test layers (unit + integration/end-to-end) that don't share an import path, so fixing the unit test doesn't guarantee the integration test was caught.

How to apply: after removing/changing a behavior, run something like `grep -rn '<old signature>' tests/` (or the equivalent old field/string) across the whole test suite, not just the file adjacent to the code change, before running the full deploy gate.

grooming-as-design-session.body:
When a task involves a new architectural pattern (pluggable nodes, protocol boundaries, extension points), run /task-grooming first and treat it as a design session, not just a checklist audit. Create subtasks for unresolved design decisions before touching code.

**Why:** task:686136ce grooming surfaced 3 pluggable-design gaps (protocol contract, registration mechanism, slot policy). Converting them to subtasks forced explicit resolution before implementation — the resulting code was cleaner and the docs wrote themselves from the decisions.

**How to apply:** If grooming flags "decision needed: X", don't note it and move on — create a subtask for it. The implementation subtask should activate only after all design subtasks are done. Three decided questions is worth one clean implementation over three mid-implementation pivots.

hard-to-test-means-bad-structure.body:
If a test is getting difficult to write, the code structure is likely the problem — simplify the code, don't force the test.

**Why:** Encountered when patching node `__call__` was awkward due to the `wrap()` decorator in `_node_log.py` sitting between LangGraph and the node. Hard-to-patch code is tightly coupled code.

**How to apply:** When writing a test requires unusual indirection (patching internals, multiple nested mocks, bypassing decorators), stop and ask whether the production code can be restructured to make the dependency injectable or the boundary cleaner. Simplify the code first, then the test becomes obvious.

historical-task-bodies-can-describe-unbu.body:
A historical task's title/body can describe intended work that was never actually implemented, or was implemented differently than described — don't treat an old task's premise as ground truth without checking the current repo state.

Why: when scaffolding removal subtasks for epic e8c2646b from prior task titles, two of four premises were wrong: task 91dad030 ("Migrate prompt_cache from sqlite table to Obsidian vault + vault_rag index") never actually moved storage — it only added a domain-scoping column, storage stayed SQLite throughout; and task 3fb2dbc9 ("Nudge Claude to cache findings via PreCompact hook") — no PreCompact hook existed anywhere in the repo, only two unrelated PreToolUse reminders.

How to apply: [[grep-all-md-files-before-declaring-doc-removal-done]] — same principle for code, not just docs. Before implementing a removal/modification task derived from historical task descriptions, grep the current repo for the named symbols/files rather than assuming the description matches reality — this is exactly what /task-grooming's Step 1 (activation + context gathering) is for; don't skip it even when a task "looks done already" or self-explanatory.

hook-dev-mode.body:
Hook error visibility is controlled by LC_DEV_MODE in langchain_learning/config.py (field: dev_mode, default: False).

When LC_DEV_MODE=true: hooks exit with code 2 on any exception — Claude Code surfaces the error inline immediately.
When LC_DEV_MODE=false (stable/prod): hooks write error to log DB silently, no exit 2.

pre_tool_use_lc is always fail-open (no exit 2 regardless of dev_mode) — crashing it would block tool calls.

**Why:** During development, silent failures (like the stale turn=0 kwarg) went unnoticed for an entire session. exit 2 makes breakage immediately visible in the conversation.
**How to apply:** Set LC_DEV_MODE=true in ~/.claude/.env during active development. Remove or set false when hooks are stable.
hook-dev-mode.name: hook-dev-mode

hook-server-single-worker-decision.body:
Decided against per-session worker processes for the claude-hooks FastAPI hook server. It stays a single uvicorn worker (no --workers N), single asyncio process handling all sessions via keyed dict lookups in the in-process MemorySaver checkpoint.

Why: per-session isolation (one process per session) would require either sticky-session routing via a reverse proxy in front of multi-process uvicorn, or spawning/tearing down a subprocess per session — the latter reintroduces the per-invocation subprocess-dispatcher overhead the FastAPI server was built to replace. It would also fragment the shared server_memory/event-log timeline across sessions. Discussed 2026-07-25/26; user's call: complexity isn't justified by the benefit at current scale.

How to apply: don't propose splitting the hook server into per-session workers/processes unless there's evidence one session's load or a crash is actually affecting others. If that happens, revisit — but default to the current single-worker design.

hooks-paths-module.body:
All project and user-specific paths for claude-hooks live in `hooks/paths.py`.

Exports:
- `PROJECT_ROOT` — resolves from `__file__`, worktree-safe
- `HOOKS_DIR` — `PROJECT_ROOT / "hooks"`
- `DOCS_DIR` — `PROJECT_ROOT / "docs"`
- `MEM_DB` — `~/.claude/MEMORY.sqlite`
- `VAULT_ROOT` — `~/workspace/claude_documents`
- `TOOL_REGISTRY_PATH` — iCloud tool_registry.json

**Why:** Previously each module computed its own `_PROJECT_ROOT` or hardcoded `Path.home() / 'workspace/claude-hooks'`, causing static files and templates to silently serve from the wrong worktree.

**How to apply:** Any new path constant goes in `hooks/paths.py` — never hardcode paths in other modules. Import with `from hooks.paths import <NAME>`.

Run scripts/init_db.py as a module, not as a path: `uv run python -m scripts.init_db`

**Why:** Running as `uv run python scripts/init_db.py` causes `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src'` because the working directory isn't on sys.path.

**How to apply:** Always use `-m scripts.init_db` form for any script under `scripts/` that imports from `src/`.

invisible-process-principle.body:
The most efficient processes are invisible. A bulk one-shot operation (e.g. backfill 89 memories) is expensive and visible — it requires a dedicated task, user attention, and a commit. An incremental operation hooked into normal work (e.g. backfill files=NULL memories during task activation) costs nothing extra and completes naturally over time.

**Why:** Abandoned task:3aeaf2d4 (bulk memory files backfill) in favor of task:512a7587 (auto-backfill in ActivateTaskNode). The activation moment already has the richest context — task files, domain, injected memories — making it the natural place to infer file provenance.

**How to apply:** Before creating a bulk data migration task, ask: is there an existing workflow event where this data is naturally available? If yes, hook into that event instead. Prefer 5 updates per activation over 89 updates once.

langchain-subprocess-runnable.body:
LangChain pattern: wrap any stdin→stdout subprocess as a RunnableLambda.
Serialize input dict → JSON → stdin; run subprocess; parse stdout JSON → return dict.
Gives the process .invoke(), .batch(), .stream(), and | pipe support for free.
Used in C6 HookRunnable to e2e-test the UPS hook subprocess the same way Claude Code fires it.
Rule: if a program speaks JSON on stdin/stdout, it can be a typed Runnable — same interface as ChatAnthropic.

**Correction (2026-07-02):** the pipeline this tested was originally `memory_loader_lc.py` — that file no longer exists as source (only a stale compiled .pyc remains in claude-hooks/hooks/__pycache__/). It was refactored into `langchain_learning/session_graph.py` (build_session_graph(), StateGraph(SessionState)), driven via `hooks/dispatcher.py`'s `_handle_user_prompt_submit()` → `run_session()`. Same in dev/test/prod worktrees. If citing a file for the UPS pipeline, use session_graph.py, not memory_loader_lc.py.
langchain-subprocess-runnable.name: langchain-subprocess-runnable

langchain-vs-claude-code-inversion.body:
Claude Code and LangChain are complementary layers, not alternatives — they represent an inversion of control.
Claude Code: Claude IS the agent. It reasons, picks MCP tools, orchestrates. Python hooks inject context around Claude but cannot compose multi-step LLM chains cleanly. claude -p subprocess = no streaming, hard to compose.
LangChain: Python IS the agent. Claude (ChatAnthropic) is just a Runnable — a typed component with .invoke()/.batch()/.stream(). with_structured_output gives Pydantic-validated responses; RunnableParallel runs LLM calls concurrently; streaming falls out for free.
Stack: Claude Code (agentic reasoning) → MCP tools (native macOS) AND → LangChain pipeline (programmatic, Claude Haiku for narrow sub-tasks with schema contracts).
Rule: use Claude Code when you need reasoning and tool selection. Use LangChain when Python should own the orchestration and Claude is one step in a typed pipeline.
langchain-vs-claude-code-inversion.name: langchain-vs-claude-code-inversion
langchain-vs-claude-code-inversion.tags: langchain claude-code inversion-of-control architecture mcp lcel programmatic agentic,claude-hooks

langgraph-checkpointer-pattern.body:
LangGraph MemorySaver checkpointer wired into hooks/server.py. session_id maps to thread_id. UserPromptSubmit passes full _fresh_state() + event fields to establish checkpoint. PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop pass only event-specific fields — checkpointer restores the rest. prompt_id, domains, keywords, memories all retained in checkpoint across all four hook events within a server lifetime. Zero DB reads between hooks.

Checkpoint store: in-process, in-memory (MemorySaver) — does NOT survive server restarts. `~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db` is a retired SqliteSaver-era file; nothing writes to it anymore.

Why: LangServe was stateless — each invoke threw away SessionState. SqliteSaver originally made the graph the session store and was cross-process safe, but caused two corruption incidents (task:b3964f85), so it was retired in favor of MemorySaver. Learned from ACME checkpoint pattern (thread_id isolation, resume from checkpoint).
How to apply: Always pass only changed fields in non-UPS invocations. UserPromptSubmit is the only full state initializer (_fresh_state). When adding new hook logic that needs prior-turn data, read from state (it's in the checkpoint). Do not assume checkpoint state survives a server restart (e.g. /deploy) — it won't.
langgraph-checkpointer-pattern.name: langgraph-checkpointer-pattern
langgraph-checkpointer-pattern.tags: langgraph, checkpointer, MemorySaver, thread_id, session_id, cross-hook, stateful-server,claude-hooks

langgraph-node-removal-touches-3-files.body:
Removing a LangGraph node from this repo's UPS pipeline requires touching 3 files, not 2: langchain_learning/nodes/registry.py (import + NODE_REGISTRY entry), langchain_learning/session_state.py (any state fields the node owns), AND langchain_learning/session_graph.py (build_session_graph()'s node-registration list, any add_edge/add_conditional_edges wiring, the ASCII topology diagram in the module docstring, and _fresh_state()'s default for any state field the node owns).

Why: task:99365a77 (removing CacheCheckNode) initially scoped only registry.py + session_state.py; session_graph.py's own independent wiring (node list, conditional edge, docstring, _fresh_state default) was found mid-implementation and would have left a dangling KeyError on the deleted node's registry key if missed.

How to apply: when grooming or implementing a task that removes a node, grep for the node's class name across all of langchain_learning/ before writing the file checklist — don't assume registry.py + session_state.py is the complete surface.

langgraph-node-removal-touches-3-files.tags: langgraph, node removal, registry, session_state, session_graph, refactor checklist, claude-hooks, task:e8c2646b

last-validated-now-auto-stamped.body:
last_validated is now auto-stamped to datetime('now') on every memory__add/memory__add_batch call (both insert and update), as of task:514edb14. Before this, it existed in the schema (via the _NEW_COLUMNS migration) but was populated on 0/124 claude-hooks memories.

Why: there was no way to answer "when was this memory last confirmed accurate" without manually tracing files/content against git log for every staleness pass.

How to apply: to find staleness-audit priority candidates, query `sqlite3 ~/.claude/MEMORY.sqlite "SELECT name, last_validated FROM memories WHERE domain='<domain>' ORDER BY last_validated ASC NULLS FIRST"` — NULL entries are memories never touched since this fix landed (highest priority, unknown freshness), then oldest-timestamp entries next. Note last_validated bumps on ANY add/add_batch call, even one that only touches tags or fixes a typo — it is not proof the body's factual claims were re-verified against code, only that the row was written. Manual sqlite3 UPDATE (per CLAUDE.md's exposed-columns convention) is still the way to stamp last_validated during a /task-grooming or /task-introspection pass that confirms a memory accurate without editing it.
